item.title: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy presses Western allies for postwar security guarantees
item.description:
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy presses Western allies for postwar security guarantees
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says his government is seeking specific security guarantees from Western allies for post-war supportByDEREK GATOPOULOS Associated PressNovember 6, 2026, 5:58 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
KYIV, Ukraine -- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says his government is looking for specific guarantees from Western allies on how post-war security support would function when the nearly-five-year war sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of his nation finally ends.
Zelenskyy's comments in an interview aired late Thursday came after two days of discussions among allies concluded in Brussels that focused on post-war security and reconstruction, and days before planned three-way talks next week in Abu Dhabi between Ukraine, Russia and the United States, the first trilateral peace discussions since February.
While talks on the contours of peace continue, the grim reality of war remained front and center Friday in Ukraine, with more Russian drone attacks and a rising death toll from Moscow's guided bomb strike Monday on a former school operating as a humanitarian aid distribution center.
Two days of talks in Brussels discussed postwar reconstruction, funding for 2027 and security guarantees backed by the Ukrainian government’s Western allies. The meetings brought together officials from the U.S., U.K., France, Germany and the European Union, along with representatives from the World Bank and the U.S. investment group BlackRock, Ukrainian lead negotiator Rustem Umerov wrote in an online post.
“We separately discussed the threats from Russia to Ukraine and all of Europe, as well as joint steps to counter them,” Umerov wrote.
In his television interview, Zelenskyy said he wants to see tangible results.

item.title: South Africa's ruling ANC faces huge decline in support, early election results show
item.description:
South Africa's ruling ANC faces huge decline in support, early election results show
South Africa's African National Congress faces a significant decline in voter support, according to interim results from local elections held this weekByMOGOMOTSI MAGOME Associated PressNovember 6, 2026, 5:47 AM
JOHANNESBURG -- South Africa's long-dominant African National Congress party was set to lose significant voter support and control of some major cities in local government elections held this week, interim results across the country showed on Friday.
South Africans voted this week in local polls that determine which parties get to control major cities and local municipal districts that are responsible for the delivery of basic services like water, road maintenance and rubbish removal.
With 76% of votes counted nationally, the ANC had garnered nearly 31% and was lagging behind rival parties in key cities like Johannesburg, Tshwane and eThekwini.
During the last local government elections in 2021, the ANC received just over 45% of votes nationally. Its worst electoral performance was in 2024 national elections, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time.
ANC spokesperson Mahlengi Bhengu on Friday acknowledged the latest results show the party was losing significant voter support.
“We are conscious of the message that our voters, especially our historical voters, are conveying to us. And we are going to have a serious, honest and deep reflection about how to rebuild the confidence between ourselves and the people of South Africa,” Bhengu said.
The ANC has dominated electoral support in South Africa since the country's first democratic elections in 1994 but has experienced a steady decline.
It formed a unity government with the rival Democratic Alliance and smaller political parties, while at the local level it governs some cities through coalition governments.

item.title: Bus whose passengers included kids crashes in France, leaving 2 dead and 16 injured
item.description:
Bus whose passengers included kids crashes in France, leaving 2 dead and 16 injured
A bus crash in eastern France has killed one minor and one young adultByThe Associated PressNovember 6, 2026, 5:27 AM
Share
PARIS -- An intercity bus whose passengers included kids on their way to school crashed on Friday morning in eastern France, killing one minor and one young adult, French authorities said.
The Prefecture in the Ain region said one minor and one young adult were killed, while 16 people were injured, including three seriously.
Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said on X that he was heading to the site following “a serious bus accident” near the small town of Lent, in a rural area north-east of Lyon.
“An accident involving an intercity bus occurred near Lent, France, with multiple casualties reported,” the prefecture said in a statement. Emergency services and law enforcement officers have been deployed to the scene, it said.

item.title: 90-year-old Holocaust survivor dies almost a year after being shot in Sydney massacre
item.description:
90-year-old Holocaust survivor dies almost a year after being shot in Sydney massacre
A 90-year-old Holocaust survivor has died almost a year after she was wounded during the massacre of 15 people at a Sydney Hanukkah celebrationByROD MCGUIRK Associated PressNovember 6, 2026, 3:46 AM
Share
MELBOURNE, Australia -- A 90-year-old Holocaust survivor has died almost a year after she was wounded during the massacre of 15 people at a Sydney Hanukkah celebration, officials said Friday.
Romanian-born Eva Geller died Thursday night in a Sydney hospital, Executive Council of Australian Jewry director Evan Zlatkis said.
She was one of around 40 people wounded when two gunmen allegedly inspired by the Islamic State group opened fire on a crowd at Bondi Beach on Dec. 14. Fifteen victims aged 10 to 87 died. One of the gunmen, Sajid Akram, was shot dead by police at the scene.
Rabbi Aron Moss said Geller had been “strong and pretty healthy right up until the Bondi attack where she was shot.”
She had been admitted to the hospital several times in recent weeks due to surgery complications, Moss said.
“She’s a proud mother, grandmother and great grandmother. A beautiful, positive person who even in these difficult months maintained her positivity,” Moss said on the family’s behalf.
“She was told after being shot that she will never walk again by the doctors. But through sheer determination, she got back up and she did walk again,” Moss added.
She walked with a cane following the leg wound, he said.
The surviving alleged gunman, Naveed Akram, the 25-year-old son of the dead gunman, has been charged with 15 counts of murder, 43 of attempted murder and one of committing a terrorist act. He has yet to enter a plea.
It was not yet clear whether Geller’s death would change the charges Akram faces.
Police said in a statement they were awaiting advice from a state coroner, who would investigate the circumstances of her death.

item.title: Myanmar to hold by-elections in April, including in areas where fighting persists
item.description:
Myanmar to hold by-elections in April, including in areas where fighting persists
Myanmar will hold special elections next April in its first vote since this year's general election that critics said was designed to cement military ruleByThe Associated PressNovember 6, 2026, 2:40 AM
Share
BANGKOK -- Myanmar will hold special elections to fill parliamentary vacancies next April in its first vote since this year’s general election that critics said was designed to cement military rule.
The elections will fill vacancies left by elected representatives who took ministerial or government posts and will include areas previously unable to vote because of conflict. The vote is unlikely to change the balance of power in the national parliament currently controlled by the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party, but it may provide a measure of public support for the parties contesting the vote.
Myanmar has been in turmoil since the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021, triggering widespread opposition. After security forces suppressed peaceful protests with lethal force, many opponents of military rule took up arms, plunging large parts of the country into conflict.
The Union Election Commission said the April 4 by-elections will be held in 55 constituencies, including 34 seats in the lower house, five in the upper house and 16 in regional and state parliaments, according to the announcement published in the state-run Myanma Alinn newspaper Friday.
At least seven of the constituencies are in towns that the military recently recaptured from armed groups fighting against it. Some of the constituencies are in seven states and regions where armed conflicts are ongoing.

item.title: What to know about Pope Leo XIV's trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru
item.description:
What to know about Pope Leo XIV's trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru
Pope Leo XIV is returning home to the continent where he spent two decades as a missionary priest and learned to be a pastor, visiting Uruguay, Argentina and his second homeland of PeruByThe Associated PressNovember 6, 2026, 12:04 AM
Share
VATICAN CITY -- VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV is returning home to the continent where he spent two decades as a missionary priest and learned to be a pastor, visiting Uruguay, Argentina and his second homeland of Peru.
The Nov. 6-17 trip marks the longest and farthest of his papacy and is coming just three weeks after Leo underwent surgery Oct. 13 to remove a cancerous tumor from his right lung. Doctors nevertheless gave him the green light to make the trip.
Latin America still is home to around 40% of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, but the Catholic proportion of the region’s population has shrunk in recent year s and the decreases are especially notable in the countries Leo will visit.
The trip begins in Uruguay, whose secular identity and separation of church and state are so deeply entrenched that Christmas is officially “Family Day” and Holy Week is “Tourism Week.”
According to Vatican statistics, nearly 77% of Uruguay’s 3.5 million people are baptized Catholics. But more than half of all Uruguayans identify as religiously unaffiliated — the highest portion in Latin America – and only a fraction of those who identify as Catholic actually go to Mass regularly.
Leo’s itinerary includes a stop at a parish in Casavalle, a poor neighborhood on the outskirts of Montevideo plagued by drug trafficking and gang violence. The church works with national and municipal authorities on support initiatives, including housing construction and addiction recovery programs.

item.title: Officials search for the bear that killed a mother and daughter in British Columbia
item.description:
Officials search for the bear that killed a mother and daughter in British Columbia
Conservation officers are searching for a grizzly bear that killed a woman and her daughter in British Columbia, Canada, over the weekendByMARTHA BELLISLE Associated PressNovember 6, 2026, 12:04 AM
Selah Reed's family first knew something was wrong when the 20-year-old missed a routine Saturday night call with her sister.
When no one had heard from Reed or her mother, Jenny Balcarras, by the next morning, they asked the Royal Canadian Mounted Police to check on their home in Bella Coola on British Columbia's central coast. Balcarras' car was gone and the doors were locked. They found the car at a trailhead up the road, but Balcarras and Reed were nowhere to be found.
Family members across Canada and the U.S. started mobilizing. Jenny Balcarras' brother, Matt, headed north from Vancouver Island, and his brother left from Calgary. They met and drove through the night but got a call late Monday that their sister had been killed, likely by a grizzly.
When they arrived at the trailhead Tuesday morning, ready to join the search for Reed, her remains had also been found. The search was now a tragic recovery effort.
The killings of Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter happened only 3 to 4 kilometers (1.8 to 2.4 miles) from where a grizzly attacked a group of schoolchildren and teachers last year as they walked on a trail. Eleven were injured, two of them critically, in the Nov. 20, 2025, attack.
Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the Conservation Officer Service, said that aggressive bear was never captured, but officials were able to collect its DNA. Officials have set new traps in the hopes of catching the bear involved in last weekend’s attack and to learn whether it was the same bear from a year ago. They also are not sure whether more than one bear was involved.

item.title: Former pro-democracy lawmaker sentenced to 12 1/2 years in Macao’s 1st national security case
item.description:
Former pro-democracy lawmaker sentenced to 12 1/2 years in Macao’s 1st national security case
Macao pro-democracy former lawmaker Au Kam San was sentenced to 12 1/2 years in prison Friday in the Chinese city’s first national security case following a closed-door trial that raised concerns about fairnessByKANIS LEUNG Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 9:58 PM
HONG KONG -- HONG KONG (AP) — Macao pro-democracy former lawmaker Au Kam San was sentenced to 12 1/2 years in prison Friday in the Chinese casino hub’s first national security case following a closed-door trial that raised concerns about fairness.
Au’s arrest last year was the first publicly known prosecution under Macao’s national security law since it was enacted in 2009. A Macao court found him guilty of subverting state power, breaching confidentiality and establishing contact with organizations, groups or people outside Macao to commit acts endangering national security.
Critics said his case reflected Beijing’s emphasis on security and intolerance of dissent, even though Macao’s pro-democracy movement has never been as influential as that in neighboring Hong Kong.
The 69-year-old assisted and cooperated with “hostile organizations” outside Macao for a long period of time in collecting and disseminating political views laden with ideas of subverting state power and false information, according to a court statement. They conspired to incite hatred among Macao residents against the central government, with an intent to overthrow and undermine the country's fundamental system, it said.
“Although the defendant is a first-time offender and admitted to a considerable portion of the criminal facts, he demonstrated a high degree of intent. The degree of unlawfulness and the potential consequences of his crimes are both very serious," the statement said.
In a public letter, Au’s wife, Virginia Cheang, wrote that she only hoped authorities would allow his family to exchange letters with Au and visit him...

item.title: Carney unveils budget to strengthen Canada's economy as Trump's trade war continues
item.description:
Carney unveils budget to strengthen Canada's economy as Trump's trade war continues
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government unveiled a sweeping budget Thursday aimed at making Canada less dependent on the United States as President Donald Trump’s trade war reshapes the longtime allies’ economic relationshipByThe Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 5:23 PM
OTTAWA, Ontario -- Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government unveiled a budget Thursday aimed at making Canada less dependent on the United States as President Donald Trump’s trade war reshapes the allies’ economic relationship.
The budget, titled “Masters of Our Destiny,” proposes $142.1 billion Canadian (US$101.6 billion) multiyear spending and tax breaks, including incentives to attract investment and billions for energy, infrastructure and culture.
The government projects spending of $603 billion Canadian (US$431 billion) and a $62.3 billion Canadian (US$44.5 billion) deficit for 2026-27, $3 billion Canadian (US$2.1 billion) less than forecast in April.
Canada’s combined federal, provincial and local government deficits amount to 2.5% of its economy, compared with 8.5% in the United States, according to International Monetary Fund figures cited in the budget.
“The United States is upending global trade,” the budget declares.
It comes two days after Democrats swept the U.S. midterm elections, weakening Trump’s political position as the countries pursue a possible trade agreement.
The government expects Trump’s trade war to slow economic growth late this year and early next year, with the budget forecasting growth of just 1% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027.
